record.original_question: For an ideal fluid in a periodic channel T x (0,a), with initial velocity C^1-close to a plane-parallel flow whose velocity profile is increasing and convex, and with an initial vorticity level line containing a kink, can one prove that the kink persists under the Euler evolution?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on the periodic channel $\Omega = \mathbb{T} \times (0,a)$, with impermeable boundary conditions on $\{y=0\}$ and $\{y=a\}$. A plane-parallel (shear) flow is a steady solution of the form $u_0(x,y) = (U(y), 0)$, whose vorticity is $\omega_0(y) = -U'(y)$. Assume $U \in C^2([0,a])$ satisfies $U'(y) > 0$ and $U''(y) > 0$ for all $y \in [0,a]$ (i.e. $U$ is strictly increasing and strictly convex).

Let $u(t)$ be the (smooth) solution of the 2D Euler equations with initial datum $u_{\rm in}$ that is sufficiently $C^1$-close to $u_0$, and let $\omega(t) = \mathrm{curl}\, u(t)$ be its vorticity. Suppose that the initial vorticity $\omega_{\rm in} = \mathrm{curl}\, u_{\rm in}$ has a level line $\Gamma_0 = \{\omega_{\rm in} = c\}$ that contains a kink, i.e. a point $p_0 \in \Gamma_0$ at which $\Gamma_0$ is a continuous curve but fails to be $C^1$ (the tangent direction has a jump).

Question: Prove (or disprove) that the kink persists under the Euler evolution. More precisely, show that for every $t \ge 0$ the vorticity level line $\Gamma_t = \{\omega(t) = c\}$ contains a point $p_t$ at which $\Gamma_t$ is not $C^1$, and that $p_t$ is the image of $p_0$ under the Lagrangian flow of $u(t)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of persistence of vorticity kinks for 2D Euler flows near a strictly increasing, strictly convex shear in a periodic channel. Related work concerns stability and quasi-periodic perturbations near Couette flow, but does not directly address the persistence-of-kink question. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Space Quasi-Periodic Steady Euler Flows Close to the Inviscid Couette Flow
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of steady quasi-periodic stream functions bifurcating from shear equilibria near Couette flow; does not address persistence of kinks in vorticity level sets.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability/perturbation results near shear flows exist, but do not resolve the kink-persistence question.

status_evidence.title: Eleven Great Problems of Mathematical Hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems in mathematical hydrodynamics; persistence of singular features of vorticity level lines remains among unresolved fine questions.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys list this circle of questions as open.
